title: (No AI) OpenAI drops another batch of mathematical breakthroughs
author: Robert Hart
content:
![Sam Altman speaking in front of OpenAI logo](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/gettyimages-2297765991.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

OpenAI has [revealed solutions](https://openai.com/index/sharing-ai-progress-in-mathematics/) to a number of long-standing mathematics problems produced by an unreleased frontier model in [a batch of 722 manuscripts, covering 372 result families](https://github.com/openai/math) that group related papers. It extends a run of breakthroughs that have both impressed and unsettled parts of the mathematical community while raising questions about research ethics and academic conduct. According to AGMAI, the [newly formed independent advisory group of elite mathematicians](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/999167/openai-elite-mathematicians-panel) put together to work on communicating the results responsibly, the release includes solutions to "hundreds" of open questions.

title: (No AI) We can’t just change the definition of ‘recording’
author: Victoria Song
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/268639_Meta_Adventurer_glasses_AKrales_0005.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

With AI hardware, tech companies are pushing the definition of what does and _doesn't_ constitute a recording. For most of gadget history, it'd be reasonable to assume that a device with a microphone or camera is either recording you or it isn't; it's either on or off, without much gray area. Microphones capture sound. Cameras capture images. That data is saved onto a device. Sometimes, it's also sent to the cloud - hopefully with end-to-end encryption - for processing. That data is a preserved instant in time and is therefore a recording.

Perhaps not anymore.

Last week, _Bloomberg_'s Mark Gurman reported that Apple is working on [a smart hom …](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1003877/apple-security-camera-no-video)

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/column/1005697/we-cant-just-change-the-definition-of-recording)
